pr_title: Fix System.DirectoryServices.Protocols to work on Linux
pr_body:
Fix #66243 

LdapPal.CompareDirectoryEntries on Linux does not pass strValue to Interop.Ldap.ldap_compare

This fix always converts CompareRequest.Assertion to byte array

issue_context.title: System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.CompareRequest fails on Linux when invoked with string attribute value
issue_context.body:
### Description

Using `CompareRequest (string distinguishedName, string attributeName, string value)` always fails on Linux. 

`LdapPal.CompareDirectoryEntries` from [LdapPal.Linux.cs](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/3ede8095da51d5d27a890020b61376155e9a61c2/src/libraries/System.DirectoryServices.Protocols/src/System/DirectoryServices/Protocols/Interop/LdapPal.Linux.cs#L15) does not pass `strValue` parameter to `Interop.Ldap.ldap_compare` from [Interop.Ldap.cs](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/3ede8095da51d5d27a890020b61376155e9a61c2/src/libraries/Common/src/Interop/Linux/OpenLdap/Interop.Ldap.cs#L256)

### Reproduction Steps

```csharp
        [TestMethod]
        public void Test1()
        {
            var server = new LdapDirectoryIdentifier("db.debian.org", 389);
            var connection = new LdapConnection(server);
            connection.AuthType = AuthType.Anonymous;
            connection.SessionOptions.ProtocolVersion = 3;
            var response = connection.SendRequest(new CompareRequest("dc=debian,dc=org", "dc", "debian"));
            Assert.AreEqual(ResultCode.CompareTrue, response.ResultCode);
        }
```

### Expected behavior

Should not fail

### Actual behavior

Fails with error DirectoryOperationException: A protocol error occurred

```
  Error Message:
   Test method CompareRequest1.UnitTest1.Test1 threw exception:
System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.DirectoryOperationException: A protocol error occurred. A protocol error occurred.
  Stack Trace:
      at System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.LdapConnection.ConstructResponseAsync(Int32 messageId, LdapOperation operation, ResultAll resultType, TimeSpan requestTimeOut, Boolean exceptionOnTimeOut, Boolean sync)
   at System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.LdapConnection.SendRequest(DirectoryRequest request, TimeSpan requestTimeout)
   at System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.LdapConnection.SendRequest(DirectoryRequest request)
   at CompareRequest1.UnitTest1.Test1()
```

### Regression?

_No response_

### Known Workarounds

Use `CompareRequest (string distinguishedName, string attributeName, byte[] value)` by converting string attribute value to byte array 

```csharp
        [TestMethod]
        public void Test2()
        {
            var server = new LdapDirectoryIdentifier("db.debian.org", 389);
            var connection = new LdapConnection(server);
            connection.AuthType = AuthType.Anonymous;
            connection.SessionOptions.ProtocolVersion = 3;
            var response = connection.SendRequest(new CompareRequest("dc=debian,dc=org", "dc", Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("debian")));
            Assert.AreEqual(ResultCode.CompareTrue, response.ResultCode);
        }
```

Thanks for the report @psteniusubi . I haven't looked into it, but if the fix is local and understood would you consider offering a PR with a test?

@danmoseley - yes I'll put together a PR. The fix is local. This needs an integration test but I think I know how to do that in [DirectoryServicesProtocolsTests.cs](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/b1da321d184875040bd6aa8c5ebd904e8192815f/src/libraries/System.DirectoryServices.Protocols/tests/DirectoryServicesProtocolsTests.cs)

review_comments:
```suggestion
                        byteArray = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(str);
```
? Avoids the extra allocation.

Hi @gfoidl. Thank you for your comments. I'm following style and conventions elsewhere in this component. More specifically implementation of BuildAttributes method:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/d64b8af65e7eecc52bf81d40315fa80c64c818c1/src/libraries/System.DirectoryServices.Protocols/src/System/DirectoryServices/Protocols/ldap/LdapConnection.cs#L1277
What happens if the bytes were not utf8 encoded?
CompareRequest operation returns ResultCode.CompareFalse. I added a test case for this.

Right, but I guess my question is: should we support that? Or is it expected that bytes will always be UTF8 encoded? I quickly looked at our [docs](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.directoryservices.protocols.comparerequest.-ctor?view=dotnet-plat-ext-6.0#system-directoryservices-protocols-comparerequest-ctor(system-string-system-string-system-byte())) and we don't seem to mention anywhere that the bytes need to be UTF8 encoded.

I don't want to block your contribution on that, if we think UTF8 is what should be expected then we can just update our docs to point that out, and perhaps consider in the future add another constructor to CompareRequest that takes in bytes[] and Encoding.
String values are always utf-8 encoded on the wire (per [ldap spec](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4511#section-4.1.2)). The byte[] value is as-is on the wire.
Sounds good, we can update the docs then to call this out, but we can do that separately from your PR

Looks like the test you are adding is only covering when the assertion is a string. Can you please turn your Fact into a Theory instead that uses both string and URI in order to make sure we have coverage for both?
Hi @joperezr. Thanks for your comments. I have changed my integration test to Theory and added more test cases.
Can we also add a tests that ensures that this Argument Exception gets thrown?
I had a look at this. Turns out DirectoryAttribute rejects other value types than string, Uri and byte[]. So this condition never happens.
I wonder if `byte[] byteArray` is needed or if this can be stackallocated (and the copied)?
This code follows how BuildAttributes method does the same conversions. I don't think improving this is within scope of this fix.

> improving this is within scope of this fix.

You are right, that's going beyond the fix.

The code here seems pretty old, and was written before span came around. So there could be a general overhaul -- but I don't know the plans here and if it is worth, as such an upgrade comes with cost and this code seems to be battle-tested, which a re-write has to prove first.
I don't think we should stackalloc this particular array since it is based on user input, so we want to make sure that we don't call stackalloc from arbitriary input size.
Using something like Marshal.StringToCoTaskMemUTF8 could save one allocation. But as I said I don't think this should be within scope of this fix.
